label: soco55 peryear gas basis
definition: SOCO-55 RECIPE: the SOCO-54 keeper recipe plus ONE delta, gas_basis_differential_measured_by_year = true. Every SOCO gas unit prices on the delivered-gas basis measured on the receipts of THE YEAR BEING SOLVED, instead of one year's value applied to all of them. WHAT WAS WRONG: GAS_BASIS_DIFFERENTIAL['SOCO'] = 0.64 is the 2024 value, and the constant's own comment registers it as a 'forward-year / fallback value only' on the ground that the SOCO backcast prices gas per plant off EIA-923. SOCO-54 made that sentence false by turning gas_plant_monthly_fuel_pricing OFF, which promoted the declared FALLBACK onto SOCO's PRIMARY backcast gas-pricing path, so resolve_annual_gas_price returned gas_price_override + 0.64 in every year. Measured, the basis is +0.4931 / +0.6395 / +0.6540 for 2023 / 2024 / 2025, so 2023 was carrying +0.15 $/MMBtu — about +$1.65/MWh — on every SOCO gas unit. SOCO-54 DECLARED that imprecision against itself and ROUTED the repair; this run is that repair. SOURCE, not residual (rule 23 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE]): quantity-weighted EIA-923 Schedule-2 delivered gas to the run's own EIA-860 SOCO gas fleet minus the Henry Hub annual mean, re-derived at HEAD and reproducing SOCO-20's committed comment exactly, registered at the 2dp every other GAS_BASIS_DIFFERENTIAL row carries — a convention fixed before the solve. ZERO free parameters (n_residual unchanged at 1); ONE new default-off ScenarioConfig gate, registered in _CACHE_KEY_OPTIONAL_FIELDS at False in the same commit as the field, so no pre-existing cache key moves. The measured table carries a SOCO row and nothing else (rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]), so every peer ISO and every forecast year falls through to the scalar unchanged — machine-verified. Rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH] at two grains: only the six GAS classes move on fuel_prices and mc_base; coal, oil, nuclear, hydro, wind, solar and biomass are at max |delta| exactly 0.000000000000 in all three years. SOLVED ONE SHARD PER YEAR (rule 36 [R-YEAR-ISOLATION]) and composed at zero LP. 2024 IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE KEEPER on all eight artifacts — dispatch/2024_P1.parquet and floors/2024_P1.npz included — because at 2dp the 2024 measured basis equals the scalar, which the PRECOMMIT pre-registered as P5. WHAT IT DELIVERS, AND IT IS AGAINST THE RUN: the 2023 residual gets LARGER. CT_PEAKER 10.668 -> 11.413 TWh (actual 4.503; share +2.56 -> +2.87pp of a +/-3.00pp cap), COAL_PRB 21.722 -> 20.443 (22.151), CC_REGULAR 112.126 -> 112.312 (107.960); only ST_GAS improves, 3.986 -> 4.293 (10.442). Every row still PASSES and C1 stays 13 of 14 with the same single failing row, 2024 CC_REGULAR at +7.505 TWh of +/-7.47, which this run is provably inert in. RULE 14 [R-ACCURATE] IS WHY THE INPUT IS KEPT: a worse fit after an accurate input is a DISCOVERED BUG, not a reason to revert. WHAT IT LOCALIZES: 95 % of the 1.279 TWh coal displacement is ONE plant, 6002 James H Miller Jr (15.838 -> 14.626 against a 15.701 actual), and about half the energy it sheds lands on merchant turbines already far above their own actuals (55409 Calhoun +0.115 against 0.026; 55061 Tenaska Georgia +0.111 against 0.238; 7709 Dahlberg +0.109 against 0.243) while the other half lands correctly on 2049 Jack Watson (+0.147 toward 3.270) and 728 Yates (+0.087 toward 2.239). The named successor is therefore the CT_PEAKER / COAL_PRB merit order, not the gas basis. C2 / C4 / C6 / C8 PASS; 0 ledgered and 0 protective caveats; rule 17 [R-FLOOR-WINDOW] holds in all fifteen plant-years. SOCO has NO price benchmark and never will, so C3a / C3b / C3c are UNSCORABLE, not failed, and no price level, shape or tail is certified. Evidence: docs/handoffs/PRECOMMIT-soco-55-2026-09-20.md, docs/handoffs/FINDING-soco-55-2026-09-20.md.
